sorted_list_to_bst.description: Convert a sorted doubly linked list into a balanced BST with the same inorder contents, reusing its nodes. Previous/next links become left/right children; the selected language contract specifies the node fields. The supplied count is the actual list length.
constraints: A nondecreasing doubly linked sequence and its actual nonnegative length; node previous/next links are repurposed as child links.

examples.output: Tree root 5 with inorder [−6,−1,5,12,19]; adapter verdict true.
examples.explanation: For sorted list [-6, -1, 5, 12, 19], build the first two nodes as the left subtree, consume 5 as root, and build the remaining two nodes as the right subtree. The resulting tree has root 5, left root -1 with left child -6, and right root 19 with left child 12. Its inorder contents remain [-6, -1, 5, 12, 19]; the adapter verdict is true. Return a tree root, not a Boolean. The JSON case contains only the sorted values; the adapter constructs the list and passes its length, then verifies inorder and returns true.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Build prefix sums and their suffix minima. For each moving start/end threshold, ask whether some endpoint at or beyond the current end can give sum ≤k; advance the end when feasible, otherwise advance the start.
checks.correctness: For a start a, the minimum prefix sum from b onward minus the prefix before a is the minimum sum attainable with an endpoint at least b. If this exceeds k, no extension from a can work and discarding that start is safe. Otherwise a qualifying interval of length at least b−a+1 exists, so this length is a valid lower bound and b can advance. Both pointers move only forward, and every longer possible answer is eventually considered.

checks.actualAlgorithm: Compute existing all-pairs shortest paths with Floyd–Warshall. For each candidate edge, test both directions of using it once for every city pair and sum the savings. Replace the best only for a strict improvement, preserving the first proposal on ties.
checks.correctness: Floyd–Warshall establishes the shortest existing distance between every pair. Any shortest path improved by one new nonnegative undirected edge can use that edge at most once, in either direction; testing those two possibilities therefore finds its new distance. Summing pair savings compares proposals correctly, and updating only on a strict improvement preserves the first proposal on ties.
checks.workedTrace: With highways (0,1,8),(1,2,8), existing pair distances sum to 8+8+16=32. Adding (0,2,3) reduces the sum to 8+8+3=19, saving 13. Adding (0,1,4) gives 4+8+12=24, saving 8. Choose proposal (0,2,3).
checks.edgeCases: An empty proposal list returns (-1,-1,0). A proposal may duplicate an existing road with a smaller distance. Equal total savings choose the earliest proposal. Long arithmetic stores path distances and total savings.
checks.timeDerivation: O(h+n³+p·n²): initialize h roads, run three nested Floyd–Warshall loops, then score each of p proposals on O(n²) city pairs.
checks.spaceDerivation: O(n²) for the all-pairs distance matrix; proposal scoring keeps only running savings and the best proposal.

When a new value arrives, each subset of the larger prefix either excludes it and is already present, or includes it and is formed uniquely by adding it to one old subset. Thus every subset appears exactly once after all values are processed.
